messages:
Riley Gomez: Heads upAcme Health procurement insists on Azure Marketplace invoicing only. They want a 12-month reserved commit for 120M tokens/mo, plus a POC on dedicated instances. How do we reconcile marketplace flows with Dedicated/Private deployments?
Priya Nair: quick take: Marketplace public offers can't provision Dedicated automatically. We can do an Azure Private Offer (APO) that lists the committed SKU and still invoice via marketplace, but provisioning Dedicated requires a separate SOW and provisioning ticket. Procurement usually accepts APO + SOW.
Marco Silva: finance note: Azure takes a ~12% take-rate on marketplace transacted revenue. That means to hit the customer's target net price we either need to increase the customer-facing discount in the APO or absorb part of the take. Both have margin implications.
Riley Gomez: procurement wants the marketplace invoice to flow to their AP system. They also need the invoice to be addressed to their parent entity. Any blockers there?
Legal Ops: changing the billed-to name on marketplace invoices is limited. Azure's marketplace invoicing must match the purchasing tenant data. We can request a custom invoice name in APO but need Azure marketplace support approval. Its not guaranteed.
Priya Nair: example math: list token price $0.00065. Customer target net $0.00050 (approx 23% off). If Azure takes 12%, our net becomes 0.000572 unless we increase the APO discount. To hit 0.00050, APO must present larger discount so post-take customer price equals target.
Marco Silva: Deal desk: if we absorb >4% of take to preserve price we escalate to CFO. Also need GL code mapping for marketplace SKUs so procurement can reconcile invoices.
Riley Gomez: timeline: Acme needs paperwork by Thursday COB to book spend this quarter. Can we put together APO + SOW + PO template in 48 hours?
Billing Bot: @Riley Gomez send the final SKU list, Azure tenant ID, and PO template to billing@redwood.com. I'll start an APO draft. Estimated APO prep time: 24 business days after submission.
Priya Nair: I'll draft two options for the packet: (1) Direct contract with deepest net price but separate invoice (slower procurement acceptance), (2) APO with price parity to direct contract if we offset take-rate (requires CFO sign-off if >4%).
Marco Silva: Also confirm POC acceptance criteria and provisioning lead time. Dedicated pool provisioning typically takes 5 business days after SOW. If APO lead time overlaps, we may meet their timeline.
Riley Gomez: action: I'll collect tenant ID and PO template and loop in procurement. Priya + Marco, please get the pricing scenarios and CFO escalation ready. Legal Opscan you advise on billed-to flexibility in APO?
Legal Ops: will ping our marketplace rep. Also note: any custom refund or extended payment terms may require contract amendments and legal review.
Priya Nair: I'll have the pricing sheet and recommended approach by EOD tomorrow. Includes a column showing our margin post-take and the net for the customer.
Marco Silva: tagging finance analyst to map SKUs to GL codes. Also need to know if the customer requires tax-exempt handling.
Riley Gomez: thanks team. If deal-desk approves absorbing 2% of take we can match their target price and likely close this week. If not, procurement will decide between longer direct contract or higher price on marketplace.
Billing Bot: confirmed received items: SKU list + tenant ID + PO. Next step: create APO ticket once items are in billing inbox.
Riley Gomez: will send those items now. Thanks everyone. :pray:
